intent: Give any repository a single repo-agnostic ship command that carries a branch from working copy to confirmed release and back to a clean, up-to-date integration branch, plus a Companion Ship tab that reports that pipeline's real state.

FR-001.title: Detect whether the working directory is inside a version-controlled repository before acting

FR-002.title: Detect the integration branch from repository configuration, under any name

FR-003.title: Ask and remember when the integration branch is ambiguous

FR-004.title: Verify remote, reachability, and credential scope before changing state

FR-005.title: Refuse to run from the integration branch, detached HEAD, or an unfinished rebase/merge

FR-006.title: Present a preflight summary of the detected profile and intended actions

FR-007.title: Stage and commit outstanding work, showing what will be committed first

FR-008.title: Publish the branch to the configured remote and establish tracking

FR-009.title: Open a pull request into the target branch, adopting an existing one instead of duplicating

FR-010.title: Compose the PR title and body per the configured mode, drafted descriptions reviewed first

FR-011.title: Wait for automated checks with progress reporting and a bounded wait limit

FR-012.title: Treat an undetermined checks outcome as unresolved and never merge on it

FR-013.title: Require explicit developer confirmation before merge and before release

FR-014.title: Release only after merge, reporting release outcome distinctly from merge outcome

FR-015.title: Never report a release as complete based on the merge alone

FR-016.title: Classify failures as conflict, check failure, precondition failure, or unresolved

FR-017.title: Retrieve and present the failing check's own output

FR-018.title: Detect an unmergeable branch before merging, update from target, resolve, re-check

FR-019.title: Attempt repairs within a bounded budget, re-entering checks after each

FR-020.title: On halt, leave branch and PR intact and report every attempt and the remaining failure

FR-021.title: Resume from the furthest stage reached rather than restarting or duplicating

FR-022.title: Detect and refuse a second concurrent run against the same branch

FR-023.title: Delete the branch locally and remotely only after confirmed merge; report a refused deletion

FR-024.title: Switch to the integration branch and update it from the remote as the final stage

FR-025.title: Never delete a branch with unmerged commits; report them instead

FR-026.title: Record each run's stages, outcomes, and timings to a per-repository state file

FR-027.title: Stamp every recorded value with its capture time

FR-028.title: Record an explicit undetermined marker with a reason instead of an inferred value

FR-029.title: Tolerate a missing, unreadable, or incompatible state file without aborting the run

FR-030.title: Ship tab shows local, published, PR, checks, release, and changelog state

FR-031.title: Ship tab shows the capture time alongside every value

FR-032.title: Ship tab renders undetermined state as undetermined, never as a placeholder

FR-033.title: Ship tab shows an explicit empty state distinguishable from a zero value

FR-034.title: Ship tab marks stale state and offers a refresh

FR-035.title: Ship tab reflects in-progress stage changes without an editor restart

FR-036.title: Ship tab renders unbacked controls as visibly disabled with the reason stated

FR-037.title: Developers can set source and target branch; runs honor the saved values

FR-038.title: Developers can choose manual, commit-assembled, or auto-drafted PR descriptions

FR-039.title: Developers choose observed or executed release mode for the repository

FR-040.title: Validate configuration on save, name the problem, retain the previous configuration

FR-041.title: Store ship configuration per repository, travelling with the repo

FR-042.title: Keep pipeline and Ship tab separable, each degrading honestly without the other

FR-043.title: Preflight detects the release mode, asking once and recording it when undeterminable

FR-044.title: Observed mode watches the repo's release path; no confirmation within the limit is undetermined

FR-045.title: Executed mode runs the configured release action and reports a failed release as such

expectations: Hosting services other than GitHub — the description names GitHub explicitly
Obtaining, storing, or rotating hosting-service credentials
Configuring or authoring the repository's automated checks — the tool consumes whatever already reports
Bypassing branch protection, required reviews, or required signatures
Serializing concurrent ship runs — a second run is refused, not queued
Repositories whose integration branch feeds several independent release targets — reported as unsupported, not partially released
A persistent always-yes setting for merge and release — unattended authorization is per-run only
context: Repository discovery: branch names, remotes, and release paths vary per repo, so nothing may be assumed
Safety posture: merge and release are outward-facing and hard to reverse, so both are gated
Truthful state: every value the Ship tab shows must trace to recorded state or be labeled undetermined
SpecKit Companion tab conventions — the Ship tab follows the existing per-repository JSON state-file pattern
Bounded automatic repair: unbounded auto-fixing on a shared branch is unsafe, so the budget is small and configurable
Resumability: a partially completed run leaves a published branch and open PR that a re-run must adopt
Release mode resolved by user decision: detect per repository, support both observed and executed
Feature scope resolved by user decision: pipeline and Ship tab both in scope, tab prioritized last and kept separable
approach: Ship the pipeline as a SpecKit extension package at .specify/extensions/ship/ mirroring the installed Companion's shape, with all deterministic stages in a Python 3 stdlib engine and command markdown owning only the two AI steps (drafting a PR description, proposing a check-failure repair). GitHub is reached through the gh CLI behind one HostingClient seam, with a preflight capability probe instead of version trust. The engine writes a per-repository state.json that a separate VS Code extension reads and never writes, making the pipeline and the Ship view genuinely separable.

decisions.decision: Read PR checks by polling `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup`, never `gh pr checks`
decisions.why: Measured on the installed gh 2.4.0: `gh pr checks` accepts only -w/--web — no --json, no --watch. Those flags arrived in far later releases. `gh pr view --json` does list statusCheckRollup, mergeable, mergeStateStatus and mergeCommit, so one call serves checks, mergeability and the merge SHA.
decisions.rejected: Building on `gh pr checks --json --watch`, which would have failed on the very machine this plan was written on; and calling the GitHub REST/GraphQL API directly, which would force this feature to hold a token the spec puts out of scope.

decisions.decision: Deliver the Ship surface as a separate VS Code extension contributing a view into the SpecKit activity-bar container, not as a tab inside SpecKit Companion
decisions.why: alfredoperez.speckit-companion@0.31.1 declares four views and no extension point, and its spec-detail tabs are compiled strings inside dist/webview/spec-viewer.js. Those tabs are also scoped to a single spec while ship state is per-repository, so even with an extension point the tab bar would be the wrong home. The spec says the tab sits alongside the existing Companion views, and those are sidebar views.
decisions.rejected: Forking the Companion (would make our pipeline depend on shipping a competing build of someone else’s extension) and waiting on an upstream PR (timeline outside our control, and FR-042 wants separability regardless). Whether VS Code renders a view contributed into another extension’s container is UNVERIFIED — no precedent among extensions installed on this machine — so a spike leads that phase and the fallback is our own container.

decisions.decision: Wrap every observed value in state.json as Determined<T> — {value, determined, captured_at, source} or {value:null, determined:false, captured_at, reason} — and reject determined:false with a non-null value on write
decisions.why: FR-027 (capture time on every value) and FR-028 (no inferred value) become structural rather than per-field discipline, and SC-007 (no placeholder anywhere on the Ship view) becomes machine-checkable instead of a matter of inspection. Configuration is deliberately NOT wrapped: a config value is a human’s stated intent, not an observation.
decisions.rejected: Bare values with a sibling *_at timestamp field — the first field somebody forgets to stamp is invisible and reads as established fact, which is exactly the failure this feature exists to prevent.

decisions.decision: Split persistence: config.json committed, state.json and ship.lock gitignored
decisions.why: FR-041 requires settings to travel with the repository, so config must be committed. Run state must not be: a state.json rewritten on every ship would conflict on every merge into the integration branch, making the tool harder to use the more it is used. .specify/.gitignore already carries this exact distinction for feature.json and local-config.yml.
decisions.rejected: One combined file (the two halves have opposite sharing requirements); state under .git/ (survives no clone); state in the home directory keyed by repo path (breaks when the checkout moves, and the view would have to reproduce the keying).

decisions.decision: Correlate releases to merges by merge commit SHA, and require a non-empty `evidence` field on any release record claiming outcome:released
decisions.why: FR-015 and SC-012 forbid ever reporting a release from a merge alone. Making evidence a required, non-empty schema field means the writer physically cannot record a release it did not observe. SHA correlation also survives the named edge case of a release queued behind other releases, where time-proximity matching would attach the wrong run.
decisions.rejected: Correlating by timestamp proximity (wrong run under queueing) and inferring the release from a successful merge (the single hardest line in the spec).

decisions.decision: Resumption re-verifies the last succeeded stage against the world before trusting the journal, and distinguishes exit code 20 (classified failure) from 30 (undetermined)
decisions.why: Recorded state can be wrong — the developer may have merged the PR in the web UI between runs. Trusting the journal alone would let a run skip a stage that never happened, breaking SC-008. Separate exit codes matter because a caller that collapses failed and undetermined re-creates the exact inference FR-012 exists to prevent.
decisions.rejected: Trusting the journal without re-verification; and re-deriving everything from GitHub with no journal, which loses the run history and timings FR-026 needs for the changelog.

plan.summary: Planned SpecKit Ship as a stdlib-Python SpecKit extension driving git+gh behind one HostingClient seam, writing a Determined<T>-wrapped per-repo state.json that a separate VS Code Ship view reads; two measured findings reshaped it — gh 2.4.0 has no machine-readable `gh pr checks`, and the Companion’s tabs are compiled and closed.
